clue.text: Region of San Diego housing independent community

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in a community or social event

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SoCal is the common short name for Southern California, where San Diego lies
I is the standard abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood of San Diego is home to a self-governing community.
explanation.walkthrough: SOCAL takes I into its middle to make SOCIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Social and community both describe things done together by people living in one area, as in a social club or a community club.

clue.text: Bottomless fizzy drink and salad? Something's going to go wrong!

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, so bottomless means the final letter goes

parts.note: soda is a fizzy drink; its final letter goes
slaw is short for coleslaw, a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a bottomless soft drink and salad, sure the meal will be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's law is the British name for Murphy's law, the idea that if something can go wrong it will.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation captures the gloomy maxim that whatever can go wrong will, which is exactly the principle named.

clue.text: Location of Stow, possibly — in the chilly South?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: chilly means cold
S is the abbreviation for South

indicators.note: possibly hints that the word may be arranged some other way

parts.note: the word rearranged, placed inside the other pieces

explanation.surface: Asking where Stow is: somewhere cold in the south?
explanation.walkthrough: Stow-on-the-Wold is a market town in the Cotswolds, a hilly area of south-west England, so Stow serves both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stow-on-the-Wold is a well-known town in the Cotswolds hills of Gloucestershire, so the region is its location.

clue.text: Painful boils oddly ignored by deity

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A god takes no notice of someone's sore boils.
explanation.definitionFit: Anubis is the jackal-headed Egyptian god of the dead and of mummification.

clue.text: Spanish music lover gets nachos regularly

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone's sweetheart treats themselves to tortilla chips every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate guitar music and dance tradition of Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Praise God, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks what was heard, so a spoken form stands in for the spelling

parts.note: the Lord is God; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they heard a call to praise God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Praise God' reads as a single phrase, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, especially in formal or religious language.

clue.text: They keep an eye on huge reptiles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people or devices that watch over something
second meaning: large lizards such as the Komodo dragon

explanation.surface: Zookeepers watching over giant lizards.
explanation.definitionFit: Monitors are overseers or screens that watch, and monitor lizards are a family of big reptiles.

clue.text: Spirit shown by chap coming up with promotion

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a man's name standing for any chap; it is turned round
an ad is a promotion or advertisement

explanation.surface: A man getting a promotion shows real spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' here is not courage but a nature spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a spirit living in a river, spring or lake.

clue.text: Demanding our nose gets blown

indicators.note: something blown about is scattered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy request that we blow our nose.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome and hard to do, just as a demanding one is.

clue.text: Course alternatively routed

indicators.note: alternatively suggests the letters can be put in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A route that has been sent a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a definition in itself, since a detour is a route sent another way.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout course or path taken instead of the direct one.

clue.text: Road on which you'd pay to go off and fish

parts.note: milk that goes off has turned
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A road where you pay a fee so you can head out angling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' reads as setting out, but it means to spoil, as milk turns sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a toll road, chiefly American usage today, where drivers pay a fee to travel.

clue.text: As drunk as a fish?

parts.note: surface reading: a simile for being extremely intoxicated, like drunk as a lord
setter's reading: a fish has no limbs at all, and British slang for very drunk means just that

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a person too drunk to stand is said to have no legs; fish literally have none.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for extremely drunk, and also literally describes a creature without limbs, such as a fish.

clue.text: One such as Moses with peculiar wig covered in seaweed

indicators.note: being covered in something means being wrapped inside it

parts.note: laver is an edible seaweed

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearrangement

explanation.surface: A prophet in a strange hairpiece draped with seaweed, perhaps after parting the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Laver is the seaweed used in Welsh laverbread; 'peculiar' looks like it describes the wig's appearance but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses brought the Ten Commandments down from Sinai, so he is the classic example of a lawgiver.

clue.text: Academic rejects American films made here

indicators.note: to reject something is to throw it out, so letters are removed

parts.note: an academic, bookish person is studious
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A scholar turns down Hollywood's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic' looks like a noun for a person, but it is the adjective studious; removing US leaves STUDIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A film studio is the company and premises where movies are shot and produced.

clue.text: Nothing is changing for egg producers

parts.note: O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing
something that is changing varies

explanation.surface: Nothing alters for the hens laying eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is changing' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovaries are the female reproductive organs in which egg cells are produced.

clue.text: You and I are going to be in good health

wordplay.words: You and I are going to
wordplay.note: you and I are we, and are going to is will, so this is the two-word contraction of we will with its apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cheerful promise that both of us will get better.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore apostrophes, so WE'LL and WELL are the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well means healthy and not ill, as in asking someone whether they feel fine.

clue.text: Guile demonstrated by cold and nerveless criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A calm, icy crook shows great cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the cool customer, but it is the anagram signal applied to nerveless.
explanation.definitionFit: Guile is crafty intelligence, and cleverness covers that sense of being sharp and cunning.

clue.text: Carrying out river excavation, core removed

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so the middle letter is taken away

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a cutting is a channel dug through ground for a road or railway; its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: Workers digging out a riverbed, with the central section taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: CUTTING has seven letters, so its core is the fourth, a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Executing a plan means carrying it out or putting it into effect.

clue.text: Creature yielding beastly blubber, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: beastly suggests brute and blubber is fat; swapping their first sounds gives the result

explanation.surface: An animal that produces disgusting fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap BR and F between BRUTE FAT to get FRUIT BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit bat is a large bat that feeds on fruit, so it is a kind of creature.

clue.text: The cruise finishes here, there's nothing left to try

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: the final holiday resort a cruise ship calls at
second meaning: the only option remaining when all else has failed

explanation.surface: A weary traveller at the end of a voyage admits defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the phrase into its plain words: the final seaside resort on the itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: A last resort is the final course of action open to someone once every other attempt has failed.

clue.text: A romance I arranged with Alison

indicators.note: arranged means put in a particular order, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they set up a love affair with Alison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A romance' begins the clue as though it were the subject; with its article it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret or illicit love affair between two people.

clue.text: Star, very mature, making a comeback

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to mature is to age; this piece is turned round

explanation.surface: An ageing celebrity staging a return to the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, which the comeback supports, but it is a star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and one of the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: Might it remove brilliant colour?

parts.note: ace means brilliant or excellent
a tone is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: A question about what would strip off bright paint or polish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: acetone is the solvent in nail polish remover, which takes bright colour off.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a strong solvent used in nail varnish remover and paint stripper to dissolve coloured coatings.

clue.text: One skins up to get unconscious

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to skin fruit is to peel it; this piece is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone rolls a joint to get knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skins up' is slang for rolling a cannabis joint, but here the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep is in a state of sleep and so not conscious of their surroundings.

clue.text: Golden couple providing home-help

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A glamorous celebrity couple supply domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreign person who lives with a family and helps with childcare and housework.

clue.text: That's the point of spin — no flipping good

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of spin

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A complaint that public-relations spin is no blooming use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed tine of a fork, so it is literally a point.

clue.text: Once more adopt desperate measures

indicators.note: something desperate is wild and reckless, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Resorting again to drastic steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassume is to take up again, so it matches adopting a role or position a second time.

clue.text: Crystalline compound extracted from cure-all

indicators.note: something extracted from a word is drawn out of the inside of it

parts.note: the letters run inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A chemical drawn from a miracle remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a colourless crystalline nitrogen compound found in urine and used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Dribbling burglar, not the first apprehended by cunning

indicators.note: someone apprehended is caught and held, so this piece is held inside the other

parts.note: sly means cunning; it goes around the other piece

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a burglar is a robber; its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A drooling housebreaker is caught by a crafty detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning' sits at the end looking like a description of the burglar, but it is the outer shell of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobbery describes something wet with saliva, so a slobbery mouth is one that is drooling.

clue.text: Sheep kept by farmer in outhouse

indicators.note: something kept by the following words is held within them, so the letters run across those words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps a sheep in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino is a breed of sheep prized for its fine, soft wool.

clue.text: Last drink which could go to your head

definitions.text: Last drink which could go to your head

parts.words: Last drink which could go to your head
parts.note: surface reading: the final alcoholic drink of the evening, strong enough to make you tipsy
setter's reading: the word also names a soft hat worn in bed, which literally goes on your head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to your head' is the idiom for alcohol making you dizzy, and also the literal place a bedtime hat sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is both an alcoholic drink taken just before bed and a cloth cap formerly worn while sleeping.

clue.text: A planetoid's orbit getting excessively extended, primarily here?

definitions.text: A planetoid's orbit getting excessively extended, primarily here?

indicators.note: primarily suggests first of all, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.words: A planetoid's orbit getting excessively extended
parts.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: An astronomer asking where an orbiting body strays farthest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the point where an orbit is most stretched out.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the point in an orbit farthest from the body being circled, where the path is most extended.
